Column: LISTING_STATUS
Table: RENTAL_INFORMATION

Short description
- Current public status of the rental listing that indicates whether and how the property is being marketed or has been taken off the market.

Purpose / Business meaning
- Used to track the marketing lifecycle of a rental unit so applications and business processes (search, reporting, lease workflows, availability calendars, analytics) can determine whether a property is active, under offer, leased, withdrawn, etc.

Suggested data type
- CHAR(2) or VARCHAR(20) (or an enumerated type / lookup FK to a LISTING_STATUS_CODES table)

Typical allowed values (examples)
- ACTIVE — Listing is currently available and being marketed
- PENDING — An application/offer is under review; unit not yet confirmed as leased
- LEASED — Unit has been leased; tenancy confirmed
- HOLD — Temporarily not accepting new applications (e.g., repairs, inspections)
- WITHDRAWN — Listing removed by owner/agent before leasing
- EXPIRED — Marketing period ended without lease
- CANCELLED — Listing cancelled for administrative reasons

Recommended implementation
- Use a constrained set of values (ENUM or foreign key to a status lookup table) to ensure consistency.
- Maintain a status history table or timestamp fields (e.g., STATUS_UPDATED_AT) if tracking status changes over time is required.

Business rules / notes
- Only one listing record should be ACTIVE for a unit at a time (enforce via application logic).
- Transition rules may apply (e.g., ACTIVE -> PENDING -> LEASED or ACTIVE -> WITHDRAWN).
- Nullability: NOT NULL with a default value such as 'ACTIVE' or 'WITHDRAWN' depending on business preference.
- Consider pairing with fields like AVAILABILITY_DATE, LISTED_DATE, LEASE_START_DATE to clarify timing.

Example value
- 'ACTIVE' — the unit is currently available for rent.
